scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot structure using Si (high-index) and SiO2 (low-index) dielectric layers can achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm with adequate stopband blocking at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, provided both materials have validated dispersion data across the full 3.6-5.2 μm operating range.
expected_advantages: Si/SiO2 is a widely available material pair in thin-film databases
High index contrast reduces required layer count for adequate blocking
20 layers provides margin below 24-layer constraint for potential refinement
known_risks: Si may have absorption features in mid-IR that reduce peak transmittance
SiO2 dispersion data may not extend to 5.2 μm in some registries
Dual-band optimization may require more than 2 cavities for adequate separation
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise more slowly than Route 1 due to lower index contrast requiring more precise thickness control
tightest_margin may be lower than Route 1 if stopband depth is insufficient with 12 pairs
valid_candidates should remain high as Si3N4/MgF2 are low-loss dielectrics
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin remains below 0.1 for four consecutive rounds, reduce pair count to 11 and add matching layers at substrate interface
